title: API Gateway authorization middleware (RBAC v2) + standardized 403s + authz metrics
creator: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description:
Background
- As part of RBAC v2, we need consistent, enforceable, deny-by-default authorization at the platform edge (API Gateway) for all security-relevant routes.
- Current state (RBAC v1 + ad-hoc checks):
  - Some routes check permissions in downstream services, some don’t, and error semantics vary.
  - Missing checks are hard to detect and regressions are easy (streaming routes especially).
  - We lack consistent telemetry for allow/deny rates and authz latency.

Goal
Implement an API Gateway authorization middleware that:
1) Enforces RBAC v2 permission checks (deny-by-default on annotated routes).
2) Standardizes error responses for permission denied (403) vs unauthenticated (401) vs not found (404) with a consistent payload contract.
3) Emits metrics and logs sufficient for rollout safety + compliance evidence (decision, reason codes, latency, cache hit-rate where applicable).

Non-goals
- Not implementing a full policy engine inside the gateway. The gateway should call the shared evaluator client/library.
- Not designing the entire permission catalog (tracked in ENG-18241 + Confluence inventory).
- Not changing identity/SSO behavior; this is authorization only.

Scope
In-scope
- Gateway middleware/interceptor for HTTP + streaming routes (SSE/websocket-like streaming) used by Redwood API + Console-backed APIs.
- Route annotations / config to specify required permission(s) + resource scope extraction.
- Standardized error schema and mapping.
- Telemetry:
  - Counters for allow/deny by action + scope type + caller kind (user vs api_key/service).
  - Authz evaluation latency (p50/p95/p99), gateway overhead, and evaluator error rate.
  - A separate metric for “missing annotation / attempted access to unannotated sensitive route” (should trend to zero).

Out-of-scope
- Fine-grained ABAC rules; RBAC v2 only.
- Customer-exposed policy debugging tools beyond a safe denial reason code and an admin-only debug header (separate ticket/PR but referenced below).

Design notes / decisions
- Enforcement location: Gateway performs the check for request admission, and services still enforce for defense-in-depth where feasible. This ticket delivers the gateway side.
- Deny-by-default:
  - Any route marked as “requires_authz=true” MUST also specify a permission.
  - If a request hits a “requires_authz=true” route and permission evaluation cannot be performed (e.g., evaluator down, malformed scope), default is DENY with reason=EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE or SCOPE_INVALID.
  - For routes not yet migrated, keep existing behavior behind feature flags (see Rollout).
- Error semantics (standard contract):
  - 401 unauthenticated: missing/invalid authn, include error_code=UNAUTHENTICATED.
  - 403 forbidden: authenticated but not authorized, include error_code=PERMISSION_DENIED.
  - Error payload includes:
    - request_id
    - error_code
    - message (safe, user-facing)
    - denial_reason_code (safe subset; detailed reasons only for admins)
    - required_permission (optional; admin-only / behind debug flag)
- Streaming routes:
  - Must enforce authorization before the first byte is streamed.
  - Ensure middleware runs prior to stream upgrade / SSE begin.

Implementation plan
1) Middleware skeleton in gateway:
   - Extract subject (user/api_key/service token) from authn context.
   - Extract required permission from route annotation.
   - Build resource scope:
     - org_id (always if known)
     - project_id/env_id/cluster_id where applicable (best-effort; deny if required and missing)
   - Call policy evaluator client.
   - Convert decision to allow/deny.
2) Standardized errors:
   - Gateway returns the canonical error schema; downstream services should avoid re-wrapping.
   - Add mapping layer for legacy errors to reduce client-side breakage during migration.
3) Metrics + structured logs:
   - Metrics names (proposed):
     - gateway_authz_requests_total{decision,action,scope_type,subject_type}
     - gateway_authz_eval_latency_ms{action}
     - gateway_authz_denials_total{action,reason_code}
     - gateway_authz_errors_total{stage}
   - Structured log event (sample fields): request_id, subject_id, subject_type, action, scope, decision, reason_code, policy_version (when available), evaluator_cache_hit (if exposed).

Acceptance criteria
- Middleware enabled (flagged) for:
  - Redwood API management endpoints (key rotation, key create/delete, org/user/role management routes proxied by gateway).
  - Console-admin routes that mutate security settings.
  - At least one streaming endpoint has explicit coverage and regression test.
- Standard error payload returned for permission denied from gateway.
- Metrics emitted and visible in dashboards; deny spikes are observable by action and reason.
- Integration tests cover:
  - Allowed request path
  - Denied request path
  - Evaluator unavailable -> deny + reason code
  - Streaming route denies before streaming starts

Rollout plan (high-level)
- Stage 0: Land middleware + metrics, flag default OFF.
- Stage 1: Enable for internal dogfood org(s) + staging; monitor deny rate/latency.
- Stage 2: Enable for pilot customers (Dedicated + Private POC) with close Support/SecEng monitoring.
- Stage 3: Gradually increase coverage; add CI guardrails to prevent new sensitive routes without annotations.

Links
- GitHub PR (middleware + deny-by-default): sources/github/redwood/pr-28159-gateway-authz-middleware-deny-by-default.json
- GitHub PR (debuggable denial reason codes + optional header): sources/github/redwood/pr-28241-add-denial-reason-codes-and-debug-header.json
- GitHub PR (feature flags + dual-read to support rollout): sources/github/redwood/pr-28315-rbac-v2-feature-flags-and-dual-read.json
- Confluence (authz enforcement patterns): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authorization-check-patterns.json
- Related incident/hotfix (streaming route bypass regression): sources/github/redwood/pr-28391-hotfix-permission-check-bypass-on-streaming-route.json
- Related tickets:
  - ENG-18241 Permission inventory / endpoint audit
  - ENG-18305 Control plane endpoint permission annotations
  - ENG-18339 Authz decision audit logging (downstream audit log schema)

Open questions
- Do we treat missing org_id for certain public endpoints as deny or allow? Current proposal: if route requires scoped permission, missing required scope fields => deny with SCOPE_INVALID.
- Final list of denial_reason_codes that are safe to expose to non-admin end users (Security Eng + PM to finalize; see Slack thread on standardization).
comments: 2025-01-24 (Amara Diallo): Drafted middleware interface in gateway. Using route annotations: required_permission + scope_resolver. Concern: some routes currently infer org_id from body; we should standardize on path/header where possible to avoid parsing request bodies in gateway.
2025-01-28 (Jordan Lee): +1 to keeping policy evaluation out of gateway. Please call evaluator client; ensure timeouts are short and failure mode is explicit deny (not allow) when evaluator errors.

2025-02-03 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Please align error contract with Console needs for 'why denied' UX. Even if we don’t expose required_permission broadly, we need stable denial_reason_code for Support to triage.

2025-02-07 (Marcus Lin): Deny-by-default requirement: any evaluator failure must be DENY. Add metric to alert on evaluator error rate so we can distinguish real denies from infra issues. Also: ensure we do NOT log raw tokens/claims.

2025-02-12 (Ethan Park): Reminder: services will still enforce for defense-in-depth. Gateway should not be the only check. But gateway should provide consistent client error semantics to stop the current 500/404/403 mix.

2025-02-18 (Amara Diallo): PR up for middleware + standardized 403 payload. Added streaming preflight hook so authz runs before SSE starts. Added p95 latency metric for evaluator call and total middleware overhead.
2025-02-25 (Leila Farouk): Added integration tests for allow/deny and evaluator unavailable path. Found a missing streaming regression test; added to suite and blocked merge until passing in CI.
2025-03-03 (Fiona McCarthy): SecOps request: add alert on sudden increase in gateway_authz_denials_total with reason_code=EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE (could indicate evaluator outage).

2025-03-07 (Amara Diallo): Merged middleware PR. Flag default OFF in prod, ON in staging. Dashboard created: Authz (Gateway) - allows/denies/latency. Next: coordinate staged enablement with Connor + Naomi.
2025-03-10 (Connor O'Brien): Rollout plan: enable for internal dogfood orgs first, then pilot accounts. Please ensure we can flip per-environment and per-org (not global).

2025-03-14 (Amara Diallo): Marking Done for this ticket. Follow-ups created for expanding annotation coverage and tightening CI guardrails. Streaming endpoint bypass incident is tracked separately and hotfix landed.
